vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.6.5

The skill bundle is a runtime security plugin for OpenClaw agents, designed to prevent data exfiltration, credential theft, and command injection. The `SKILL.md` and `references/details.md` are highly transparent, detailing network behavior, data handling, and even providing instructions for users to verify provenance and monitor network traffic. The `activate.mjs` and `status.mjs` scripts perform documented actions: registering the agent with `https://www.openguardrails.com/core` (sending only agent name/description) and storing/retrieving an API key in `~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json`. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unauthorized data exfiltration, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the agent itself. All actions align with the stated purpose of a security plugin.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements, instructions, and included scripts are coherent with a runtime security plugin that offers local protections and an optional cloud activation; nothing requested is disproportionate to that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (runtime security guard) match the observed behavior: local-only protections implemented in-plugin, optional registration/activation with openguardrails.com for cloud behavioral checks. The only external interaction is a clearly documented register/POST to https://www.openguardrails.com/core and later detection calls, which is consistent with the described 'cloud' component.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the two scripts only instruct running the included Node scripts, installing the npm plugin via the OpenClaw CLI, and optionally performing a provenance audit. The scripts only read/write the credentials file under ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/ and make network calls to the documented CORE_URL. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate message contents.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec embedded in the skill bundle; the documented install path uses openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard (npm). This is an expected mechanism for a plugin but carries normal npm-package trust considerations — the SKILL.md correctly instructs users to verify npm ↔ GitHub provenance before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables and requires only creating a credentials.json under the user's home OpenClaw credentials directory when the user opts into activation. That credential is proportional to the documented cloud registration/activation purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false; the skill is user-invocable. The only persistent change is writing its own credentials file under ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/, which is consistent with its stated activation flow. It does not modify other skills' configs or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it claims: a local-first security guard with an optional cloud component. Before installing/activating: 1) verify the npm package matches the GitHub source using the npm pack + diff steps suggested in SKILL.md; 2) inspect the included scripts (activate.mjs/status.mjs) yourself — they are short and readable; 3) only run activation if you trust https://www.openguardrails.com/core, since activation registers the agent and writes an API key to ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json; 4) if you need high assurance, perform activation from a monitored environment (mitmproxy/tcpdump/Little Snitch) to confirm only sanitized metadata is sent; and 5) if you later distrust the service, delete the credentials file and revoke the key via the portal. If you want extra caution, install from a locally audited clone of the GitHub repo rather than directly from npm.
